curriculum.lesson_evidence: A geography unit review and showcase revisits liveability skills: criteria, evidence, comparison and recommendation. Students select strongest work, explain the method, and identify one skill to improve. Showcase language stays evidence-based rather than decorative.
curriculum.scope_limit: Proposed Stage 4 NESA HSIE alignment using catalogue outcome code GE4-1; content-point mapping remains pending. Local First Nations protocols and Community verification remain pending human review. Do not invent Country names, Dreaming stories, sacred knowledge or unverified cultural claims.

lesson.child_mission: A geography unit review and showcase revisits liveability skills: criteria, evidence, comparison and recommendation. Students select strongest work, explain the method, and identify one skill to improve. Showcase language stays evidence-based rather than decorative.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write a three-part showcase note for this unit: best skill shown, evidence type used, and one improvement.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: names a geography skill, points to evidence type, and gives a specific improvement (not “try harder”).

WATCH FOR
Rewriting the whole unit as a story with no criteria or sources.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Independently build a short showcase portfolio page: one map or table excerpt (described), one paragraph explaining criteria→evidence→claim, and a reflection with one measurable skill goal for the next inquiry.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

teach_steps.explain:
A geography unit review and showcase revisits liveability skills: criteria, evidence, comparison and recommendation. Students select strongest work, explain the method, and identify one skill to improve. Showcase language stays evidence-based rather than decorative.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a detail is uncertain, identify what source you would need next. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
